paragraphs: 5 former Mustangs appeared in professional games on Saturday for 5 clubs across 2 levels, with Andrew Alvarez producing the night's most notable performance.
Andrew Alvarez started on the mound for Washington Nationals.
Andrew Alvarez worked 7.0 innings, allowing 1 hit and 0 earned runs, with 4 walks and 8 strikeouts.
One of his strikeouts came in the fifth on a 1-2 93 mph four-seam fastball, when he put away Kyren Paris.
Washington Nationals beat Los Angeles Angels, 6-5.

Bryan Woo started on the mound for Seattle Mariners. He worked 6.0 innings, allowing 3 hits and 0 earned runs, with 2 walks and 5 strikeouts. One of his strikeouts came in the third on a 2-2 97 mph four-seam fastball, when he put away Lawrence Butler. Seattle Mariners beat Athletics, 19-1.

Steven Brooks came on in relief for Portland Sea Dogs in the top of the eighth with nobody out. He worked 2.0 innings, allowing 0 hits and 0 earned runs, striking out 4 without issuing a walk. One of his strikeouts came in the eighth on a 3-2 pitch, when he put away Jamari Baylor. Portland Sea Dogs beat Binghamton Rumble Ponies, 1-0.
Brooks Lee went 2-for-3, 1 run scored for Minnesota Twins. He batted second and started at third base. Minnesota Twins beat Cleveland Guardians, 4-3.
Zach Daudet went 0-for-3 for Corpus Christi Hooks at Double-A. He batted seventh and started at third base. Corpus Christi Hooks fell to Midland RockHounds, 1-6.
title: Andrew Alvarez turns in a strong outing on the mound
